synthesis.executive_summary: Cross-paper synthesis for 'Compare attention mechanisms and vision transformers for autonomous perception' indicates convergence toward attention-driven architectures while highlighting persistent computational bottlenecks on edge hardware.
key_findings: Vision Transformers utilize multi-head self-attention mechanisms [Ref-1] in 2024 to capture global spatial dependencies.
Empirical benchmarks on nuScenes [Ref-2] in 2025 demonstrate superior 3D bounding box mAP for ViTs.
However, Convolutional Neural Networks maintain lower memory footprints and latency on edge hardware [Ref-2].

research_gaps.title: Real-Time Edge Quantization of Vision Transformers
research_gaps.description: Existing ViT architectures lack 30+ FPS real-time execution on resource-constrained automotive ECUs.
research_gaps.unexplored_aspect: Post-training mixed-precision quantization specifically tailored for self-attention matrices.
research_gaps.suggested_investigation: Evaluate INT4 quantization on transformer attention heads with minimal mAP degradation.

hypotheses.statement: Applying mixed-precision INT4 quantization to attention blocks preserves >=98% baseline mAP while doubling edge inference FPS.
hypotheses.null_hypothesis: INT4 quantization degrades perception accuracy by >10% with negligible latency improvement.
hypotheses.experimental_protocol: Benchmark mAP across nuScenes test split using TensorRT with calibrated activation scales.
hypotheses.expected_outcome: Statistically insignificant accuracy drop (<1.5%) with a 2.1x speedup on edge hardware.

trend_analysis.dominant_trend: Attention-based Transformer architectures superseding pure CNN backbones
trend_analysis.growth_trajectory_rationale: Exponential increase in transformer publications for real-time perception tasks.

decision_support.trade_off_analysis: Sacrifices ~5.7% mAP accuracy for a 3x speedup in inference latency.
Achieves peak mAP accuracy but requires dedicated hardware acceleration.

future_directions: Investigate hardware-software co-design for sparse attention mechanisms on edge accelerators.
Explore self-supervised pre-training strategies on unlabeled multi-modal driving logs.
Establish standardized safety validation frameworks for attention-based perception errors.
